Steps.Message:
Our staff have now arrived on site in the Blawith Road area. They will start running tests at our substation to see how the local network is operating.

It's quite common for power to be restored briefly and go off again; this is our engineers using testing equipment to energise different sections of our network - this helps to narrow down any possible issues.

Our cabling network is often broken down by smaller sites, and our staff may also check these to test for any problems, and they may also walk the cabling route to see if there are any signs of malfunction that have appeared on the surface. Our time frame hasn't been adjusted, so for now I'll let you know more news as soon as our staff update us.

Sent by Decasta at 19:51 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Austen and Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations. If you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Kevin at 18:50 - We believe our engineers have been able to restore power to all 405customers in the Tunbridge Wells TN3   area by diverting power around an underground network fault. We're pleased that we have been able to restore power sooner than we estimated.

If your power isn't back on, we'll need to hear from you. To report this, or to talk to us about anything else, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

We know that being without power can be worrying, but please rest assured that our staff work around the clock to keep the lights on. If you have any concerns or questions, give us a call any time.

What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Simon at 17:51 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an underground network fault affecting 405 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 22:30 and 23:30. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

PlannedIncidentReason: We're carrying out planned work in your area. For our engineers to carry it out safely they need to turn the power off. We're doing this work as it's essential to provide reliable electricity supplies to your area. We're sorry for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience.
MainMessage: We have repaired the problem with the electricity supply in your area. There may still be some tidying up to do, and any details have been passed to our Maintenance department, who will attend to it as soon as possible. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

Steps.Message:

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Sometimes we can't restore everyone this way, so we're also sending staff to check our equipment. Sent by Simon at 10:56 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Sevenoaks area should be back on. The issue was caused by debris on our overhead cables, which our engineers have now safely removed to restore power. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.

MainMessage: We have repaired the problem with the electricity supply in your area. There may still be some tidying up to do, and any details have been passed to our Maintenance department, who will attend to it as soon as possible. Steps.Message:
Sent by Simon at 10:45 - Our engineers have identified a section of network that has been damaged by fallen trees. They are currently diverting as much power around this section as possible. However, due to the location of the damage, we will not be able to restore all customers this way.

Therefore, we plan to restore some supplies by connecting a temporary generator. The remaining properties will be restored by diverting power around the network.

We're still estimating we'll have power back on between 13:30 and 14:30. Some properties may be back on sooner than others but we'll keep you updated.

Sent by Will at 01:39 - I'm pleased to confirm that all power in the Chilthorne Close area should be back on. The issue was caused by an unexpected underground cable fault, which our engineers diverted power away from by reconfiguring the network cabling.

If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Will at 01:09 - Our digging team are progressing well with excavations to expose our cabling so repairs can begin. Excavations can sometimes take longer than expected, depending on ground conditions, other utility equipment like gas and water pipes, parked vehicles, or local traffic.

At the moment our estimated time frame of 03:00 and 04:00 hasn't changed, but as our staff are busy working with live electricity we need to wait until they can safely stop work and contact us with the latest information. Once they do, we'll update you further.

Our team are always here if you have any questions.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Sent by Simon at 10:14 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Thank you for your patience while our team worked hard to resolve this issue safely; we're pleased that our engineers were able restore the power within the timeframe we had estimated.

If your power isn't back on, we'll need to hear from you. To report this, or to talk to us about anything else, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Sent by Kevin at 08:45

Hi. I'm sorry that an engineer hasn't arrived in your area yet. 

Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy wind and rain, and all our available staff are travelling from area to area to get as many customers restored as possible. We appreciate that your power may have been off for a long time and we're sorry for the disruption this must be causing you. As they are arriving later than expected, we're now aiming to have power back on between 11:30 and 12:30.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to call us on 08003163105.

Sent by Talie at 05:47.

Sent by Talie at 04:43 - Our engineers are on their way. We believe the issue is an overhead cable fault that initially interrupted power to 477 properties.

However, we have managed to divert power back to some properties, so 64 properties are still affected. Specialist engineers from our control room will continue to divert power remotely, so your power may come back on at any point. Sometimes we can't restore everyone this way, so we're also sending staff to check our equipment.

We're currently estimating power will be on between 05:30-06:30, but this may change depending on what our staff find.

Power back on? To stop receiving texts, follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Otherwise, we'll keep you updated.

Steps.Message:
We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
As a result of this. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 15:30 and 16:30. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Kevin
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Talie at 04:55 - Hi - thanks for bearing with us, I know a power cut can be very disruptive. We've had an update from our staff that there are now 25 properties still affected by the overhead cable fault, as they have managed to safely divert some power, which has restored power for some of our customers. Further specialist engineers will be required this morning to patrol the overhead cabling in daylight and at the moment, we don't need to change the estimated timeframe. We'll keep sending text updates to everyone until all the power to your area is on. To stop receiving texts, just follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Our engineers have arrived on site in the Dereham, NR20 5 area to investigate the power cut affecting 348 properties. Specialist engineers are also working to divert power remotely, and this can cause your lights to go on and off. We know that a power cut can be very disruptive, even more so if you are vulnerable. If you're worried about an elderly or ill person in your property who is affected by the power cut today, we are able to provide some support. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress but for any concerns or questions, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. For more information on how we support vulnerable customers just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR

Sent by Talie at 03:46 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Norwich, NR15 1 area should be back on. The issue was caused by overhead cable fault, which our engineers have now diverted power around. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Simon at 06:35 - We're very sorry we've had to switch off your electricity. Our engineers have turned off the power in the Dartford DA4 area in the interest of the public's health and safety. This is so they can investigate reports of a low overhead line.

If in the area, please take care and stay at least 10m away from the cable. 

Until our engineers arrive on site and investigate, it's difficult to advise you a time frame. However, based on an average for this kind of issue, our estimated time to have you back on is between 18:30 and 19:30 

We'll keep you updated with our progress, but in the meantime our team are always here to talk on 105 if you have any questions or concerns.

Steps.Message:
We're sorry your power has gone off again.

We believe there may be an underlying issue causing the recent power cuts, but due to the nature of the electricity network, the heat created by a developing fault can cause a break in a cable to reseal itself. This can make it difficult to locate, so while our engineers are testing our equipment thoroughly to pinpoint the issue, this kind of problem may interrupt power multiple times before it's possible for us to fix.

We know that our customers may be worried about the food in the fridge and freezer, so we want to try and help with advice. Food should keep for up to 4 hours in the fridge, and between 24-48 hours in the freezer if you avoid opening them.

I'll keep you updated. Sent by Jack at 09:58

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

Our staff have found a potentially dangerous situation involving low hanging overhead cables so have responded as quickly as possible and asked our control room to turn power off to the area using our high voltage network. This is why a wide area has lost electricity.

Our field teams are working to fix the issue as quickly as possible, and we'll start diverting power back to affected homes as soon as they advise us it's safe. You may notice your lights going on and off as we work to get as much power restored as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Simon at 10:51- Engineers are still on their way to investigate the cause of the voltage issues in the Rochester area.

We appreciate that power flickering and lights dimming can be concerning. Usually, this is due to interference with cabling and can sometimes cause network safety equipment to partially operate, meaning not all power is coming through to your property as normal.

Also in some cases we have to restore power in stages; so it's normal to continue receiving messages for a while even after your power has come back on.

We'll be in touch again when we arrive on site.

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.
